_doc: Per-scanner-model table for the Android bridge (ScannerModel.java; bundled as assets/scanners.json by the
Gradle build). How to add or fix a model:
docs/adding-a-scanner-model.md. Keys under 'models' are the scanner's USB PID (VID 0x2BC5).
A model entry is merged over 'defaults' (objects merge key by key, lists and values replace).
'inherit': '<pid>' merges another model first. A local override file (files/scanners.json in the app's
private dir) is merged over this whole document.
interfaces: USB interface number (Windows MI_xx) of the UVC VideoControl interface that carries each stream,
or [vc, n] for its n-th VideoStreaming interface (two streams on one VC), or 'auto' to guess from interface
names using auto_interfaces. V4L2 fourccs are 4 chars, space padded.
status: verified (tested end to end) | partial | unverified (from RE only, never run) | unsupported (the app
won't use it behind a bridge) | unknown. Evidence tags in notes: [O] observed in code, [I] inferred, [?] unknown.
Only the CR-Scan Otter and CR-Scan Ferret Pro entries are verified on hardware; the others come from static

Y16._note: cameraServer drops Y16 from 0xFC1 (not in its fourcc table); the client could parse it

RLE._note: BlockStdDevCompression V3 (RleCodec.java), produced from Y8 by the bridge (ir_synth)

0x06DA.name: CR-Scan Otter
0x06DA.notes: MI_02 IR = IR/IR_LEFT, MI_00 Depth = DEPTH/IR_RIGHT, MI_04 RGB, MI_06 HID IMU (248-byte reports).

0x0C04.name: CR-Scan Otter Lite
0x0C04.notes: Same SDK class as the Otter (AvatarDevice), so the client expects the Otter layout [O client]. The official bridge supports it.

0x0C09.name: CR-Scan Otter Lite Basic
0x0C09.notes: AvatarDevice, Otter layout [O client]. The official bridge bundles its firmware (1.0.1/1.0.2).

0x06A8.name: CR-Scan Raptor
0x06A8.notes: Interfaces and modes as listed by the scanner (fw 1.3.8, issue #15) [O]: IR GREY/MJPG 480x300 (MI_00 only) to 1920x1200, Y14 depth on MI_00, color MJPG/YUYV up to 1280x800. Props 0xC5/0xC6 (line scan left/right = the IR frame light type filter, 0xFFFF = all) are answered by the bridge, as cameraServer does; the scanner refuses them outside its line-laser work modes [O SDK]. ir_light_types: libOrbbecSDK's PioneerIRFrameRawDataCallback table [O], keyed by the first SCR byte of each frame's UVC payload header, where Orbbec scanners put per-frame data (the Otter's IR frames carry 0xA2/0xFF there, both keys of this table [O]); that this is the byte the SDK reads is [I]. PioneerDevice uses the default port bytes = Otter layout [O client]. cameraServer adds MJPG and RLE copies of Y8 IR [O]. The client decodes BlockStdDev RLE only if fw int >= 10107, else MidRleNeon (not implemented), hence ir_synth_min_fw [O], with fw 'a.b.c' -> a*10000+b*100+c [I]. Default IR_L/R 1920x1200@50 Y8 (~115 MB/s per eye) [O XML]: Wi-Fi needs RLE and/or lower fps. Fixed fc1_order copied from the Otter [I].

0x0C00.name: CR-Scan Raptor X
0x0C00.notes: PioneerDevice, see 0x06A8. Bridge XML default IR_L/R is 1920x1200@50 RLE [O].

0x0C11.name: CR-Scan Raptor Pro Max
0x0C11.notes: Client treats it as PioneerDevice [O]. The official bridge (fw 1.3.1) can't open it and has no RLE entry for it, so these settings are copied from the Raptor Pro [I].

0x0C05.name: Sermoon X1
0x0C05.notes: Line-laser class: no IR or DEPTH sensor; IR_LEFT and IR_RIGHT both come from infIndex 0, COLOR 2, HID 4 [O client]. That the two IR streams are the first and second VideoStreaming interface of VC 0 ([0,0]/[0,1]) is [I]; needs lsusb -v. cameraServer skips the 0x70/0x12 sets and uses JPEG q90 for this PID [O]. In the 'Laser Lines Big Fov Scan' / 'Laser Lines Fast Scan' work modes it streams native MJPG IR instead of a synthesized copy [O].

0x0C06.name: Sermoon S1
0x0C06.notes: Line-laser layout like the X1 [O client; two-VS split I]. cameraServer: MJPG + RLE IR copies, no 0x70/0x12 sets [O].

0x0C0B.name: Creality Pika
0x0C0B.notes: Unsupported: a self-contained wireless scanner (Creality Scan's 'wireless interconnection' mode, like the Sermoon P1/P1S) that no Scan Bridge serves. App name RAPTOR_PIKA. Line-laser layout [O client]. Not in the official bridge SDK. Client IR chain: TurboJpeg + BlockStdDev RLE [O]. Pre-stream props are cameraServer's generic default [I].

0x0C10.name: Elegoo M1 Ultra
0x0C10.notes: Unsupported: Elegoo's handheld all-in-one scanner (built-in Wi-Fi and processing, launched Oct 2026), not a Creality one. Creality Scan's SDK knows the PID and builds it like the Pika [O]; listed only so the app recognizes it. Not in the official bridge SDK.

0x0C08.name: Sermoon P1
0x0C08.notes: The client's bridge (combo) device rejects P1/P1S [O]; they connect over their own network mode instead. IR RLE is a different codec (BlockRle, 4x4, not decoded).

0x069C.name: CR-Scan Ferret
0x069C.notes: Default port bytes = Otter layout, Avatar-like IR chain [O client]. The official bridge SDK knows the class, so it probably works there [I]. XML default depth is 1280x800@30 RLE from the device (flavour unknown), not advertised here.

0x06A1.name: CR-Scan Ferret Pro
0x06A1.notes: Verified on fw 1.2.7: preview and a full scan over Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Direct (device report, GitHub issue #2). Same class as the Ferret. It has its own Wi-Fi handle that speaks the Scan Bridge protocol [O client], so it may not need a bridge.
